subject: Request: data-use exception for telemetry (Atlas Analytics)
messages:
From: Ryan Bates <ryan.bates@atlas-analytics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: lisa.hammond@atlas-analytics.com, procurement@atlas-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Telemetry data-use: exception request to retain aggregated logs

Jonas / Dev —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited about Redwood’s latency profile; a couple procurement/legal items popped up on our side that I wanted to surface early to avoid surprises.

Short version: Atlas needs a limited exception in the DPA around telemetry so we can retain aggregated inference telemetry (per-tenant metrics + hashed request fingerprints) for 18 months for billing reconciliation and model performance monitoring. We are not asking for raw customer PII or request payload storage.

What we can provide with the exception:
- Aggregated token-level metrics (per-model, per-tenant)
- Hashed IDs (one-way salted hash we control) for deduping and billing reconciliation
- Access limited to Atlas ops and a read-only analytics pipeline

Attached is a redline of your DPA (Atlas - DPA redline v3.docx) with suggested language and a short data flow diagram (data-flow-diagram.png). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a retention window of 18 months for this aggregated telemetry or whether security/legal require a shorter limit? If you can propose alternate wording we can take back to our legal team.

We’re trying to close contract by next week; appreciate quick feedback.

—Ryan
Ryan Bates
Head of Platform, Atlas Analytics
ryan.bates@atlas-analytics.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Bates <ryan.bates@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry data-use: exception request to retain aggregated logs

Ryan — thanks for the context and the redline. Looping in Product (Dev) and Security (Evelyn) to evaluate the technical necessity and the compliance angle.

High level response: Product is sympathetic — we do need aggregated telemetry to maintain model health and billing reconciliation — and Security will need tighter controls than what’s in the draft. Before we take a formal position I want to surface a few concrete asks so we’re all aligned:

1) Proposed scope: aggregated metrics + one-way hashed IDs only; no raw payloads or plaintext PII stored.
2) Retention: you’re asking 18 months. Security: wants to explore 12 months with a documented exception path. Product: prefers 18 months to support trend analysis across seasonal cycles.
3) Access & controls: read-only analytics role, IP allowlisting for exporting, and an audit trail for anyone accessing telemetry.
4) Subprocessors: we need Atlas to sign off on the list of Atlas subprocessors that will receive telemetry-derived exports (if any).

Next steps: Dev — can you confirm exactly which metrics are required and whether we can downsample to preserve utility while reducing retention needs? Evelyn — can you list the minimum technical controls you’d require to consider an 18-month exception? If we can align, I’ll send a response back to Ryan with a proposed compromise and legal-ready language.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry data-use: exception request to retain aggregated logs

Jonas / Evelyn — quick product note from the infra side on required telemetry:

What we need (minimum):
- Per-tenant token counts, error rates, median latency, p50/p95/p99 latency buckets per model version per day
- Hashed request fingerprint (salted one-way hash) for dedupe/chargeback mapping; we never need the original prompt text for billing
- Model resource usage (GPU-time) per tenant, aggregated daily

Options to reduce retention risk:
- Downsample: keep daily aggregates for 18 months, keep per-request hashed fingerprints only for 90 days (useful for dedupe/chargeback short window), then move to a keyed summary for long-term trends (12–18 months).
- Differential retention: full daily aggregates retained 18 months; per-request identifiers retained 90 days and then replaced with rolling aggregate IDs.

We can implement export controls and a read-only export role. Implementing an IP allowlist + signed export request workflow is straightforward. From product perspective, 18 months for the aggregated daily metrics is ideal; hashed request IDs for 90 days acceptable if that lets Security sign off.

Link to a short design sketch: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dpa-exception-guidance (internal).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry data-use: exception request to retain aggregated logs

Thanks — this aligns with my expectations. Security position and minimal gating to consider an exception:

Required controls for any >12 month retention ask:
- Data minimization: absolutely no plaintext request payload or PII allowed in telemetry store. Hashing scheme must be one-way with per-customer salt managed by Atlas (not reversible by Redwood).
- Access controls: RBAC with least privilege, export approvals workflow (two-person signoff) and IP allowlisting for any downstream exports to Atlas systems.
- Auditability: immutable audit logs for every access/export for the full retention window; logs must be retained outside the telemetry store (SIEM).
- Subprocessor transparency: Atlas must provide a list of subprocessors that will receive exports and accept Redwood’s subprocessors list. Any vendor not already on Redwood’s approved list requires an exception review.
- Attestations: SOC 2 Type II copy and recent penetration test summary from Atlas before we enable automated exports.

Given those controls, Security can consider 18 months for aggregated daily metrics. But per-request identifiers should be limited to 90 days. We should also gate automated exports until legal signs off on the wording in the DPA.

I attached a short checklist (security-checklist.pdf) you can send to Atlas to expedite their responses.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Trust
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Bates <ryan.bates@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, lisa.hammond@atlas-analytics.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, procurement@atlas-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry data-use: exception request to retain aggregated logs

Ryan — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. We discussed internally and think there is a pragmatic compromise that should move this forward quickly:

Proposed compromise (for legal to redline):
- Aggregated daily metrics (token counts, error rates, latency buckets, per-model resource usage): retain for 18 months.
- Per-request hashed fingerprints (salted one-way hash): retain for 90 days for deduping and billing reconciliation; after 90 days replace with a keyed summary for long-term trends.
- No plaintext request payload or PII will be stored in the telemetry system.
- Exports to Atlas: require two-person approval, IP allowlist, and exports logged to an immutable audit trail.
- Atlas to provide subprocessors list and SOC2 attestation before automated exports enabled.

Next steps:
1) Atlas: confirm you can accept the 90-day limit on per-request hashed IDs and provide the subprocessors list + SOC2 attestation by EOD Thursday (2026-12-03).
2) Redwood: we will push legal-ready DPA language if Atlas confirms. I’ve attached the redline we’ll work from (Atlas - DPA redline v3.docx) and our security checklist.
3) If Atlas agrees, Hannah (Legal) — can you assemble a short DPA amendment and we’ll route for signature (DocuSign link below).

DocuSign (prelim): https://www.docusign.com/link/ABCDEF
HubSpot: HS-12345

If Atlas can confirm the subprocessors list + SOC2 by Thursday I’ll route this to legal the same day. Appreciate the quick turnaround — we recognize your timeline to close.

Best,
Jonas
